item.title: Pakistan's embassy in Tehran refutes rumours of people 'attacking' its ambassador to Iran
item.description:
Pakistan’s embassy in Iran on Sunday refuted rumours of an attack on Ambassador Imran Ahmed Siddiqui in Tehran, terming them “baseless”.

In a post on X, the embassy said it had taken note of “certain reports circulating in social media and other forums” concerning the Pakistani ambassador to Iran.

The embassy shared a post from another X account, which had posted a video showing a commotion amongst a large crowd of people in an unidentified building, with several people appearing to engage in physical altercations.

The account that posted the video alleged, citing reports, that the Pakistani ambassador had been attacked in Tehran at an unspecified event where he had been invited. It did not specify the nature or origin of the reports.

The account claimed that Siddiqui was taken to a nearby hospital for medical treatment.

“The embassy categorically clarifies that these reports are baseless and factually incorrect,” the post by Pakistan’s embassy in Tehran said.

The ambassador himself has not made any statement on his X account about the rumours.

Pakistan appointed Ambassador Siddiqui as its envoy to neighbouring Iran in February. Before assuming his current post, he served as Pakistan’s ambassador to Bangladesh.

Last month, the information ministry refuted rumours that Pakistan’s envoy in London was “confronted and attacked with a white powder-like substance”.

It said the video being shared on social media was “fake and is being circulated with a misleading caption”.

item.title: Thousands protest in India's capital against voter roll revision
item.description:
Thousands joined a protest led by opposition politicians in India’s capital on Sunday, renewing demands for the country’s election chief to resign over an overhaul of voter lists they say unfairly benefits the ruling party.

The nationwide revision of electoral rolls has sparked political disputes and street protests in the world’s largest democracy over the last month.

The Election Commission says the initiative is necessary to ensure accurate voter lists, but the opposition claims it is being manipulated to favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

Both the Election Commission and the BJP deny the accusations.

On Sunday, protesters led by opposition Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi chanted “vote thief, leave your seat” and beat drums while marching from central parts of New Delhi to Ramlila Maidan, a large outdoor venue.

“I have been a voter since I was 18 and now I find myself struck off the list,” protester Nandita, 46, told AFP, giving only one name.

“It’s important to be here because of the way things are going. The cost of living is going up… The only option is to take to the streets peacefully.”

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online youth-led protest movement, has also thrown its weight behind the campaign against the voter-roll revision.

The overhaul of India’s voter rolls has resulted in more than 133 million names being removed from electoral lists, according to figures reported by Indian media and cited by opposition parties in court filings.

Critics say the removals have disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims.

Members of Hindu-nationalist BJP have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India’s electoral rolls.

Election authorities say the revision was intended to eliminate duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries, and that eligible voters remain entitled to apply for inclusion on the roll.

Human Rights Watch has said the removal of voters was “arbitrary and deeply flawed”.

“The authorities should immediately scrap the voter roll revision process that has denied India’s most marginalised people their right to vote and other government services,” it said in a statement this week.

The Cockroach movement has been heavily involved in the pushback to the voter-roll revision and several of its leaders were temporarily detained by police during protests last month.

The CJP has gained millions of followers on social media since it was launched in May.

Earlier protests organised by the CJP in July over exam irregularities forced the resignation of the education minister, marking a rare climbdown by Modi’s administration.

item.title: West Indies crush Bangladesh by eight wickets in Mirpur Test
item.description:
West Indies defeated Bangladesh by eight wickets in the Mirpur Test on Saturday, chasing down a target of 170 with ease to take a 1-0 lead in the two-match series.

Bangladesh, led by Najmul Hossain Shanto, failed to put up a fight after setting the visitors a modest target. West Indies reached 170-2 in just 35.1 overs, with Brendon King and Kavem Hodge guiding them to victory.

King remained unbeaten on 81, while Hodge finished on 31 not out off 27 balls. John Campbell also made a valuable contribution with 49.

The ease with which West Indies chased the target was in stark contrast to Bangladesh's batting performance on the same pitch. The surface had offered considerable turn to the West Indies spinners earlier in the day, making it appear a spin-friendly wicket.

However, Bangladesh's spinners, Taijul Islam and Mehidy Hasan Miraz, failed to replicate that success. They struggled to bowl consistently in the right areas, allowing King and Campbell to attack without giving the bowlers much opportunity to settle into a rhythm.

Bangladesh had scored 272 in their first innings before being dismissed for 142 in the second. Nayeem Hasan top-scored in the second innings with 52, while Zakir Hasan contributed 22.

West Indies' spinners played a decisive role in restricting Bangladesh, with Roston Chase taking five wickets for 36 runs and Jomel Warrican claiming four for 63.

West Indies had scored 245 in their first innings, giving Bangladesh a narrow 27-run lead. But the hosts' second-innings collapse left the visitors with a target they chased down comfortably.

Hasan Mahmud took one wicket for 14 runs during West Indies' second-innings chase, but Bangladesh could not prevent the visitors from completing a convincing victory.

The result puts West Indies in the lead ahead of the second and final Test of the series on 5 November.

item.title: Saudi says intercepted ‘hostile drone’ in Riyadh region
item.description:
Saudi air defenses intercepted a drone in the Riyadh region on Saturday, according to the spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis.
“Air defenses intercepted and destroyed a hostile drone in the Riyadh region,” Turki al-Malki wrote on X, adding that “debris from the interception fell without causing injuries.”
Malki did not say who launched the drone.
In recent weeks, Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis have ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, including by launching deadly strikes on Riyadh airport that forced its closure for two weeks and the cancellation of flagship events -- threatening the kingdom’s economic diversification plans.
On Friday, Malki said the Houthis had targeted the Medina region, home to Islam’s second holiest city, but the group later denied the claim.
The Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure, airports and ships come after hostilities resumed in Yemen over the summer between the Houthis and the country’s internationally recognized government, which is backed by Riyadh.
More than 1,600 people have been killed and over 275,000 displaced since the fighting reignited, according to United Nations figures.
In July, a fragile 2022 truce fell apart after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen’s capital Sanaa in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks.
Later, the Houthis declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before seizing Yemen’s entire Red Sea coast in a lightning campaign.
The Houthis have reported frequent Saudi airstrikes in areas they control as Riyadh retaliates.

item.description:
Brandon King struck a career-best 81 not out as West Indies cruised to an eight-wicket win over Bangladesh in the first Test on Saturday to take a 1-0 lead in the two-match series.
King hit 10 fours and a six in his 115-ball knock to help the visitors chase down the target of 170 in 35.1 overs on the fourth day in Mirpur after Bangladesh were bowled out for 142 in their second innings.
Jomel Warrican, who was named player of the match, claimed 4-63 to follow up his five-wicket haul in Bangladesh's first innings as the hosts were bowled out in 48.4 overs.
West Indies captain Roston Chase took 5-36 in the second innings, his fifth five-wicket haul in Test cricket.
Bangladesh had resumed the fourth day at 79-6, holding a lead of 106, but their hopes of setting a challenging target suffered an early blow when Jaker Ali edged Warrican to slip, where Chase took the catch.
Jaker, who scored 22 off 34 balls, was the second-highest scorer for Bangladesh in the innings.
Nayeem Hasan survived two dropped catches off Chase, on 21 and 29, to keep Bangladesh going.
He added 26 runs with Hasan Mahmud before Warrican trapped the latter lbw for eight.
Taijul Islam contributed eight in a 17-run partnership with Nayeem before Chase dismissed him to leave Bangladesh at 127-9.
Nayeem then reached his maiden Test half-century off 87 balls, with four boundaries, but his resistance ended when he attempted to hit Chase over long-on and was caught by Joshua Bishop.
He made 52 off 91 balls, while Shoriful Islam remained unbeaten on seven as Bangladesh were dismissed cheaply.
West Indies started confidently, with openers King and John Campbell continuing their aggressive approach to take the visitors to 64 without loss in 14.1 overs before rain interrupted play.
After a delay of around an hour, they added another 23 runs before bad light and lightning forced a further stoppage of 45 minutes.
King was dropped on 70 by substitute fielder Ebadot Hossain off Taijul after the break, but the opener made Bangladesh pay with his fine, unbeaten knock.
Campbell fell just short of a half-century, bowled by Shoriful for 49 off 55 balls, with six fours and a six.
The second Test will be played in Sylhet from November 5.

item.title: Iran’s supreme leader warns US, Israel against new attacks
item.description:
Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against returning to war, according to a written statement, following threats from the Islamic Republic’s foes of a possible resumption of strikes.
“If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for ending them,” said a statement attributed to Khamenei posted on his website.
The remarks came during a reported meeting between Khamenei and senior military commanders, including armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi. It was the first reported meeting between them.
Khamenei has not been publicly seen since he became supreme leader, following his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s killing in US-Israeli strikes at the start of the Middle East war in February.
According to the statement, Khamenei ordered the commanders to ensure that “any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response.”
It also said that Khamenei ordered the commanders to update Iran’s target list to include “all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy.”
The war began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which swiftly responded with attacks on countries around the region.
The supreme leader’s statement came as fresh diplomatic efforts were underway to avert a resumption of fighting.
A Qatari delegation arrived in Tehran on Friday for talks with Iranian officials, after Iran reportedly received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance.
According to Iranian media, Tehran had yet to respond to the letter.

item.title: European diplomats shun Russia at G20 gathering in the US
item.description:
A Group of 20 foreign ministers’ meeting in the US city of Atlanta got off to a rocky start on Friday after top diplomats from European nations refused to take a “family photo” along with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who is hosting the gathering, decided to scrap the photo before the meeting got underway because Washington didn’t want it to become a spectacle or distraction.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul told reporters before the first session on Friday that there wouldn’t “be a family photo with European partners and Mr. Lavrov together because ... there is no normalcy with Russia.”
The two-day gathering of the G20 grouping, which includes the EU, Russia, Germany, India, China, Brazil and other major countries, is meant to be a precursor to a G20 leaders summit later this December.
That G20 leaders meeting in December is set to be hosted by US President Donald Trump at his golf club in Miami.
Rubio still opened the talks by stressing unity on major issues, telling his counterparts that they were in a “critical moment.”
“We are facing a series of interconnected economic and geopolitical crises,” he said.
He pointed to disruptions to global energy and trade and said many were posing “severe threats to essential foundations of the global economic order.”
But several countries, including the United States and Russia, are involved in separate wars. Wars in Iran and Ukraine have resulted in a spike in food prices for people around the world.
While the message is about unity and finding solutions to problems like freedom of navigation in the Black Sea and the Strait of Hormuz during the G20 meeting, the reality is that finding common ground will likely be much tougher.
Given a renewed momentum to revive talks to end the war in Ukraine, there was also interest in getting Lavrov to talk about Russia’s stance on future talks with Kyiv.
The US has invited Russian President Vladimir Putin to the G20 meeting in Miami, but it’s unclear whether Russia has accepted the invitation.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has previously said that he would be open to traveling to Miami to hold talks with Putin if he were also there.
The Kremlin has so far declined direct meetings with Zelenskyy, with Russia’s Sergey Lavrov telling DW on the sidelines of the meeting that Putin is willing to meet with the Ukrainian leader if he travels to Moscow.
“President Putin said if he [Zelenskyy] is willing to meet, let him come to Moscow,” Lavrov said. “We will guarantee his safety.”
Lavrov declined to say whether Putin will attend the G20 summit this December.
Putin has not attended a G20 leaders meeting since 2019 and only attended a session virtually in 2023.
Russia has also continued with its attacks on Ukrainian cities in recent weeks, stepping up drone strikes on water and energy infrastructure.
The European Union’s top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said ministers at the G20 meeting were able to call out Lavrov for his “lies” at the table.
“We were talking about the big geopolitical crises, including Ukraine, and we were able to address Sergey Lavrov head-on with this,” Kallas said on the sidelines of the meeting.
“Of course, he put forward a lot of lies, a lot of false narratives that we were also able to then rebuke,” she said.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband also called out Lavrov, saying, “If we are serious about our values and our interests, we must also work harder to secure just and lasting peace in Ukraine.”
Lavrov, who is under international sanctions for Russia’s war in Ukraine, was invited to the US at a time when the two countries have appeared to have fostered warmer ties.
Trump announced a diesel deal with Russia earlier this month and also waived new sanctions on Russia’s energy. The US announced the move just weeks away from the midterm elections on November 3.
Lavrov said on Friday that despite those efforts, “in practice, no real progress in relations with the US has so far been seen.”
The Trump administration has been embroiled in disputes with South Africa, having imposed visa restrictions on South Africans who it said were complicit in discriminating against white people.
Ukraine, which is not a G20 member but was invited to attend previous such meetings, was not invited this year because US officials said they made a conscious choice to include only formal members of the group.
But US officials didn’t extend that invite to South Africa, a G20 founding member and the only African country in the group.
“We have consistently maintained that our nonparticipation is not voluntary,” said Phindile Kunene, spokesperson for South African Foreign Minister Ronald Lamola.
With this many issues on the table, it appeared less likely that there would be a joint consensus at the end of the talks.
Instead of a final declaration, the AFP news agency reported, the meeting is expected to end on Saturday with a chair summary drafted by the US.

item.title: Mark Carney: Canada has ‘learned we are overdependent on the US’
item.description:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney spoke to DW on Friday after talks in Montreal with European Union leaders seeking to hammer out details of a new, closer partnership between Canada and the EU.
Amid difficult negotiations with US President Donald Trump, representing Canada’s biggest trading partner, Carney said that he and his compatriots had come to realize the country was too dependent on the economic powerhouse to the south.
“The lesson we’ve taken, Canadians as a whole, is we’re overdependent on the United States. Too closely connected to the United States. And we need to build our strength here at home and diversify and deepen our partnerships with like-minded countries internationally,” Carney said.
An EU delegation led by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa held talks with Carney and other Canadian officials in Montreal on Friday.
They’re discussing the plans floated by Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to forge what she called an “associate membership” — a status that does not yet exist for any other country — even as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s government resists creating this label. Carney seemed to speak in its favor.
“Well, I think the advantage of what we’re doing is that a few things are absolutely clear, irrespective of the exact terminology that’s used. President von der Leyen uses associated membership. We use associated membership,” he told DW’s Katharina Kroll at Port of Montreal Tower.
“What does that mean? It means the closest possible partnership without being a full member of the European Union, because Canada is not in Europe geographically and therefore cannot have accession.” Carney said.
Asked if he was looking to create a “new transatlantic bloc without the US,” Carney said it was more about diversifying and deepening Canada’s other partnerships than excluding by far its largest trading partner.
“We’re both partners of the United States, obviously close partners, alliance partners in Nato. And there are many, many opportunities for cooperation with the United States,” he said. “But in many cases, there’ll be much deeper cooperation for Canada between Canada and Europe than Canada and the United States.”
He mentioned both existing areas of cooperation like the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (Ceta), calling it “one of the most successful free trade agreements in the world,” and also pointed to research cooperation and programs like Horizon Europe and Erasmus+ enabling student exchanges.
But Carney also pointed to areas where the two sides could seek to expand cooperation, naming areas like space technologies, artificial intelligence and critical minerals.
Despite his well-documented difficulties with Donald Trump — perhaps most crudely exemplified by Trump’s attempts to unilaterally rename Lake Ontario, or his posting AI videos imagining him as an ice hockey player beating Carney up in a fight — Carney said US-Canadian ties were too deep to be derailed by any governments or prime ministers or presidents.
“The bonds between Canadians and Americans are longstanding. They’re very strong. And big elements of that will be maintained regardless of the government in Canada, the government in the United States, the combination of the two,” he said.
Asked about the best way to deal with Trump, Carney said it was “to be direct, to be clear, to be absolutely clear about your bottom lines are.” He said it was important to show respect but also to continue to bring “the negotiations back to the core issues.”
But he said the tensions with Trump had demonstrated the need to diversify and to seek Canada’s other most natural partners around the world.
He acknowledged that no matter the nature of the talks with the EU, “the scale of the relationship with the United States” would be “very hard to replace.”
Asked if he was concerned that the talks could expose him to further tariffs or other punitive measures from the Trump administration, Carney said, “We’ve been living with this for some time.”
“There have been many justifications for trade action against Canada that the United States has had,” he said. “Our view is that all of them are unjustified under our trade agreement.”
Carney said the crucial message, also for the Trump White House, was that the talks with Brussels concerned a “positive association” and partnership “to help solve global problems” and address global challenges.
“It’s not against somebody. It’s for. It’s a positive act,” he said.

item.title: Iran warns US, Israel against new attacks after Trump, Netanyahu threats
item.description:
Iran's supreme leader on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against launching new attacks following their threats to resume strikes after crucial elections, as fears mount over a return to fighting.

The declaration came as the Islamic republic's top diplomat said there were no plans to hold talks with the United States, as indirect mediation via Qatar continues.

President Donald Trump has warned of fresh military action after the US holds midterm elections early next week, saying last weekend that he was weighing whether to "finish them off".

In Israel, which is coming off fresh elections, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has spoken of a "historic, one-time opportunity" to topple the Iranian government.

Polls in both countries could determine the direction of the conflict, with Israel having voted Tuesday but yet to form a new government.

"Any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response," Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei told top military commanders in a meeting, according to a statement.

Iran says discussing plan with mediators to end war, reopen Hormuz

The encounter was the first reported meeting between Khamenei and military top brass, and included armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi.

The supreme leader has not been seen publicly since before he took the helm in March after the killing of his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in US-Israeli strikes.

Khamenei also ordered commanders to update Iran's target list to include "all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy".

Iran has previously warned it would consider severing undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz.

Petrol prices weigh on US vote

Since the initial US-Israeli strikes in February, ordinary Iranians "have been left in a state of limbo for the past year", Fariba, a Tehran housewife, told AFP.

But other residents in the Iranian capital brushed off the possible return to full-scale conflict.

"We do not fear another war. We have been at war for 48 years now," said Ebrahim, a salesman in his forties.

Since the outbreak of the war, Tehran has restricted shipping through the strategic waterway, which normally carries around one-fifth of global oil consumption.

The blockade has caused a spike in global energy prices, making the war unpopular among the US public ahead of midterm congressional elections Tuesday.

Gains for the opposition Democrats could restrict, to an extent, Trump's ability to enact policy.

Voting in Israel has left Netanyahu's political camp with the most seats in parliament but short of a majority, leaving the make-up of the next administration unclear.

'Flames of war'

The war began on 28 February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran. The Islamic republic swiftly responded with attacks on American assets in countries around the region.

Fresh diplomatic efforts are underway to avert any resumption of fighting, with Qatari mediators landing in Tehran on Friday, and US Vice President JD Vance sending a letter to Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei.

But Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday that "currently, there are no plans for meetings with American officials".

Trump rules out new Iran attack before US midterm elections

"Iran's conditions are clear, and consultations regarding them are ongoing among mediators," he said in an interview with Al Jazeera, according to the state news agency IRNA.

Qatar and Pakistan have been mediating between the warring parties, but the talks have yet to produce a lasting agreement.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Vance had sent his letter to Iran's security chief at Trump's direction in a bid to revive negotiations and avert further US strikes.

Araghchi confirmed that Iran received the letter, saying, "The American side's effort to open a dialogue and reach a broader understanding is viewed as a positive step."

But the Iranian side kept firm its warnings against further attacks.

Earlier on Saturday, army spokesman Mohammad Akaraminia said that any resumption of hostilities would only expand the scope of the war.

"The flames of war will undoubtedly engulf a much wider geographical area," he said on social media, without elaborating.

Araghchi warned on X of an "Earth-shattering blow Iran's Powerful Armed Forces will deal against those who dare harm our people".

He said there would no longer be any "red lines".

item.title: Energy and Power minister: Law on rooftop solar coming in next session of Parliament
item.description:
The government will pass a law on rooftop solar power generation in the next session of Parliament, Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood said on Saturday.
Speaking at a roundtable discussion organized by the New Age newspaper in the capital, the minister said the government was giving priority to solar power to strengthen the country’s energy security and ease pressure on conventional energy sources.
He said the energy and power crisis triggered by the prevailing global situation would not be resolved overnight, but the government was making continuous efforts to keep energy and electricity supplies at manageable levels.
The minister said the government was committed to tackling the crisis caused by the ongoing conflicts around the world, particularly the war in the Middle East, and maintaining stability in the country’s overall energy situation.
He said the government had been compelled to provide subsidies where necessary to reduce the burden of the energy crisis on consumers and protect public interests.
As an elected and responsible government, ensuring uninterrupted electricity and gas supplies to citizens was one of its key responsibilities, he said, adding that the government remained committed to maintaining normal energy supplies under all circumstances.
Iqbal Hassan said the government had also taken initiatives to establish additional Floating Storage and Regasification Units (FSRUs) or floating LNG terminals, considering future demand and the need to address supply shortages.
He said the government had launched a domestic rooftop solar programme in Bhaluka to encourage households to adopt solar power.
Responding to a question about the quality of solar panels, the minister said the government was alert and active in ensuring quality control of solar products available in the domestic market.
He said the government would maintain strict monitoring to protect consumers’ interests.
The minister said instructions had already been issued to local government institutions, health authorities and district administrations to use solar power systems.
Around 8,600 service providers have already been enlisted to install solar systems at the local level, he said.
Solar power was also creating new employment opportunities in the country, he added.
The minister said the government was standing by the people and making all-out efforts to safeguard the country’s overall energy security.

item.title: Labour minister: Wage board for garment workers to be formed Sunday
item.description:
Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury has said a wage board will be formed on Sunday to set new wages for garment workers, adding that there is no reason for workers to continue their agitation now.
The minister made the announcement at a press briefing at Shram Bhaban in Bijoynagar following a meeting with representatives of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA).
The minister said the decision to form the new wage board on Sunday was taken after five hours of continuous discussions with workers' leaders on Friday.
Noting that BGMEA and BKMEA leaders have accepted the workers' demand for a wage board, he said there should be no further dispute over the issue.
Ariful said discussions were also held with the BGMEA and BKMEA representatives on paying workers' outstanding wages, and they will talk to factory owners and take steps to clear the dues as soon as possible.
"Initiatives have been taken for forming the wage board and paying the arrears. So, there is no need for vandalism or keeping factories shut at this stage. Such activities may damage the garment industry," the minister said.
He alleged that although workers are working in different factories, some outsiders are coming in and inciting them.
The minister urged the media to showcase through video footage who the genuine workers are and who is taking part in the agitation.
He said the meeting also discussed ensuring payment of workers' wages by the 7th of every month.
However, he warned that production and supply of goods would be disrupted if factories remain closed.
"If goods cannot be delivered to buyers, owners will not receive payment, which may in turn create problems in paying workers' wages," he said.
Calling on workers to return to work, the minister said the government has taken steps to meet their demands.
He stressed that owners, workers and all stakeholders must act responsibly to maintain stability in the garment industry.

item.title: Bangladesh, World Bank ink $450m agreement for financial sector reforms
item.description:
Bangladesh has signed a $450 million financing agreement with the World Bank to strengthen the country's financial sector safety net, enhance supervisory capacity and support restructuring of the banking sector.
The financing agreement under the 'Financial Sector Support Project II' was signed between the Government of Bangladesh and the International Development Association (IDA), the World Bank's concessional lending arm, on October 30.
Economic Relations Division (ERD) Secretary Md. Shahriar Kader Siddiky and World Bank Division Director for Bangladesh and Bhutan Jean Pesme signed the agreement on behalf of their respective sides.
The project will receive 328 million Special Drawing Rights (SDR) or equivalent to $450 million and will run from July 1, 2026, to June 30, 2031.
The Bangladesh Bank will implement the project under the supervision of the Financial Institutions Division (FID) of the Ministry of Finance.
The project aims to strengthen the financial sector safety net, improve the supervisory capacity of the financial sector authorities and support restructuring of the banking sector.
Under the financing terms, the loan carries an annual interest rate of 1.5% on the withdrawn credit balance.
It also includes a maximum commitment fee of 0.50% per annum on the undisbursed financing balance.
However, the World Bank has waived the commitment fee for Bangladesh for many years, including the current FY27.
The financing has a maturity period of 25 years, including a five-year grace period.
The ERD said the World Bank remains Bangladesh's largest multilateral development partner, with its financing supporting a wide range of sectors, including economic and social development, institutional reforms, infrastructure development and energy sector advancement.
The latest financing agreement reflects continued cooperation between Bangladesh and the World Bank in strengthening the country's financial and institutional capacity.

item.title: Bangladeshi-led startup Tillion lands Y Combinator spot, outpacing a $300m rival
item.description:
Tillion, a San Francisco-based startup co-founded by three Bangladeshis, has been selected for Y Combinator's 2026 batch. Y Combinator is one of the world's most competitive startup accelerators.

Reports say only about 1 per cent of applicants get into Y Combinator, whose alumni include Airbnb, Stripe and Reddit.

Tillion's four co-founders are Md Shahrier Islam Arham, Kazi Fardinul Hoque and Abdul Basit Tonmoy of Bangladesh, and Arman Luthra of India.

The company wants AI agents to be able to work on the web as smoothly as humans do.

Much of everyday online work is repetitive: logging into many websites, filling in the same forms, copying data from one page to another. AI agents are being tested on these tasks around the world. But when thousands run at the same time, they often get stuck, held up by slow websites and unstable browser sessions.

Tillion is building browser infrastructure made just for agents. Y Combinator's profile of the company calls it “self-healing”. It can run millions of agent sessions a day with no human watching over them. If one session fails, another picks up the task and carries on.

Customers use the platform for large-scale data collection, automated workflows and round-the-clock monitoring. They can rent many browsers at once and connect them to their own systems with a single line of code.

At the heart of the technology is Fortress, an open-source engine built on Chromium, the engine behind Google Chrome.

The founders say the internet is humanity's greatest creation, yet AI agents are treated as second-class users on it. Since every agent ultimately works for a person, they argue, shutting agents out ends up hurting people.

David vs Goliath

Browserbase, a US company doing similar work, is valued at about $300 million. Tillion has just four people, yet it has topped ComputeSDK, an open and independent benchmark, several times, ranking ahead of Browserbase.

The company says engineers from more than 170 companies use Fortress. Public PyPI and Docker figures show more than 100,000 downloads. Tillion also says a $1 billion AI lab and a Fortune 500 company use its technology.

Shahrier and Fardinul said nobody expected a team this small to top the benchmark. Running thousands of agents without a single failure seemed even less likely.

The people behind Tillion

Arham has won national championships in debating, science fairs and robotics. He built software that helped thousands of students find jobs, and he built Tillion's browser infrastructure from a hostel room.

Fardinul's A-Level results placed him among the world's top students. He later worked at Amazon Web Services, where he ran hundreds of AI models on a single machine.

Luthra, an olympiad medallist, wrote the remittance algorithm behind a government budget of about $1 billion. A Washington think tank later hired him to work on complex data problems.

Tonmoy won several national olympiad titles and led NDITC, the technology club at Notre Dame College in Dhaka. At Wabash College in the US, he won hackathons, including CalHacks at UC Berkeley. He published AI research as an undergraduate. His open-source model helps robots remember what they see and hear, and one of his models ranks among the world's best on a global benchmark.

Riding the AI wave

Global investment in AI is growing fast, and demand is rising for infrastructure and developer tools as well as finished products. Tillion is part of that shift.

Tonmoy believes AI's next big leap will not be smarter answers but AI that works reliably.

The founders say that if Tillion succeeds, people will win back the hours they lose to repeated logins and form-filling. How far it gets will depend on how reliable and safe the technology proves in real use, and how well it meets customers' needs.

“We envision a world where agents do the repetitive work, and humans can dedicate their time to creativity,” said Arman Luthra.

item.title: Government forms new wage board to increase garment workers’ salaries
item.description:

item.title: Bangladesh garment workers protesting for higher wages clash with police
item.description:
Thousands of Bangladeshi garment workers blocked a major highway and clashed with police on Monday, demanding a monthly minimum wage more than double their current pay, as protests spread across industrial hubs.

The South Asian nation of 170 million people is the world’s second-biggest garment exporter behind China, manufacturing clothes for some of the largest international brands.

Hundreds of workers in Gazipur, north of the capital Dhaka, blocked the Dhaka-Tangail highway, vandalising several vehicles, while large groups took to the streets in the Mirpur district, where police dispersed demonstrators with tear gas, AFP reporters saw.

Angry workers also set fire to a police vehicle.

The protests came despite the government’s announcement on Sunday that it would establish a wage board to review the minimum wage in the vital garment industry, which employs millions of people and generates the bulk of Bangladesh’s export earnings.

However, labour leaders say workers’ grievances extend beyond the formation of the board, citing inflation and rising household expenses.

The protesters demand a 30,000-taka monthly wage, more than double their current pay.

Workers currently earn about 13,000 taka a month, according to Kalpona Akter of the Bangladesh Centre for Workers Solidarity.

Police fired stun grenades and tear gas canisters to disperse crowds in Ashulia, a Dhaka suburb and the site of some of the country’s largest factories.

“Food prices, cooking gas and electricity bills have all gone up — the government must either bring down the prices of essential commodities or raise our wages,” said Mamum, 28, a factory worker.

Machine operator Sharmin, 24, said: “We keep the wheels of the economy turning. They must listen to us.” Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed warned that the government was taking strong action to stop the protests.

“Those engaging in unlawful activities and conspiracies under the guise of labour movements will be tackled with an iron hand,” he said after meeting industry leaders on Monday.

‘Crack down’

However, Ahmed also said earlier Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had instructed officials after hosting an emergency cabinet meeting late on Sunday to “ensure workers’ rights and improve their living standards”.

He said Rahman had told them to make sure production and exports continued “unhindered”.

Bangladesh’s main manufacturer associations for garments and knitwear warned that “prolonged unrest could disrupt production, delay export shipments and affect Bangladesh’s commitments to international buyers”, the state-run BSS news agency said on Monday.

Kamrul Hasan, general secretary of the Ekota Garments Sramik Federation, told AFP some labour leaders had gone into hiding.

“We were not prepared for this unrest either, as the wage board has already been formed,” he said.

“But workers are now protesting over wages and other unresolved issues.”

In Ashulia, security officers chased protesters as they scattered down narrow side streets, with the choking tear gas drifting into densely packed housing where families often live crammed into single rooms.

“Police fired tear gas shells inside our compound,” said Kamona, 24, who gave only one name.

“We have children, but they don’t care.”

Industry representatives said workers from at least 529 factories in Dhaka and its surrounding industrial areas, including Savar, Ashulia, Jirani and Gazipur, had left their workplaces on Sunday.

item.title: Wage board set as unrest shuts Bangladesh garment factories
item.description:
DHAKA: Bangladesh said on Sunday it had set up a wage board to review garment workers’ pay and urged employees to return to work as violent protests forced the closure of more than 500 factories, with police firing tear gas and water cannon at demonstrators.

The dispute has raised concerns about widespread disruption to an industry that employs about four million workers, generates more than 80pc of Bangladesh’s export earnings and supplies clothing to many leading Western brands.

The workers in the South Asian nation are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($245), more than double the current 12,500 taka, saying rising costs of food, housing, transport and healthcare have sharply eroded their purchasing power.

“The cost of living has increased far beyond our incomes,” worker Mahin Hossain said. “After paying rent, there is very little left for food, our children’s education and other essential expenses. Many are finding it almost impossible to support their families.”

Police use tear gas

Despite the announcement of the wage board, thousands of garment workers staged demonstrations on Sunday, blocking roads in Dhaka and Gazipur, outside the capital, and disrupting transport across key industrial areas.

Police used tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters after demonstrators threw bricks at officers, and a police vehicle and a police box were set on fire in separate incidents. Authorities deployed Border Guard Bangladesh personnel to maintain order.

The latest unrest follows demonstrations in Ashulia, a major garment manufacturing hub on the outskirts of Dhaka, where dozens of factories suspended operations on Saturday after workers staged protests demanding higher pay.

In all, the unrest has forced 529 garment factories to shut down and left 987,190 workers out of work across the country’s main industrial hubs, according to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association.

Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury said the wage board was formed after discussions with workers’ representatives and industry leaders, and urged workers to resume work.

The six-member wage board comprises two representatives each from workers and employers, along with a government representative and a neutral member. The body has been tasked with reviewing wages in the garment sector and recommending revised pay rates.

Delayed shipments

Choudhury warned that prolonged disruptions could delay export shipments and payments from international buyers, creating further difficulties for manufacturers and workers alike. Bangladesh’s ready-made garment industry, the world’s largest after China, contributes about 10pc of gross domestic product and is the backbone of the economy.

Manufacturers, however, say the sector is facing mounting challenges, including rising production costs, periodic gas and electricity shortages, and uncertainty in energy markets linked to tensions in the Middle East.

Govt employees receive salaries under new pay structure after 11 years
item.description:
Government officials and employees received their salaries under the new pay structure on Sunday, along with arrears of increased salaries for July, August and September.
Many government employees received SMS notifications on their mobile phones after 10am, confirming the payment of their October salaries and the additional amounts due for the previous three months.
According to officials at the Finance Division of the Ministry of Finance, nearly all of the country's 1.4 million government employees, 800,000 pensioners and 600,000 MPO-listed teachers received the increased payments.
However, there were also employees who could not receive their revised salaries as their pay fixation process remained incomplete.
Several government officials said they received notifications confirming the payment under the revised pay structure from around 10am. They expect the remaining employees to receive their payments within the next two to three days after completing the pay fixation process.
The government issued a gazette notification announcing the new National Pay Scale on September 17, retaining the existing 20 grades of government employees while deciding to increase basic salaries by up to 142%.
Under the revised structure, basic salaries for employees in grades one to 11 increased by 100%, while those in grades 12 to 20 received increases ranging from 115 to 142%.
The new pay structure came into effect on July 1, 2026, with implementation scheduled in phases rather than through a single adjustment.
According to the notification, from July 1 to December 31, 2026, officials in grade nine and above will receive 40 percent of the increased basic salary while employees in grades 10 to 20 will receive 50% of the increase.
The additional amount has been calculated against the salaries drawn or due on June 30, 2026.
From January 1 to June 30, 2027, employees will receive 75 percent of the increased basic salary. The government will implement 100 percent of the revised pay scale, including annual increments, from July 1, 2027.
All other allowances will continue at the rates applicable on June 30, 2026, until December 31, 2027. The revised allowance rates announced in the gazette will take effect from January 1, 2028.
The previous National Pay Scale came into effect in 2015, making the latest revision the first major restructuring of government salaries in 11 years.
Under the 2015 pay scale, basic salaries increased by 95% at the highest grade and 101% at the lowest grade.

item.title: What the LDC extension means for Bangladeshi industries
item.description:
The United Nations General Assembly's decision to extend Bangladesh’s Least Developed Country (LDC) graduation timeline to November 2029 offers a crucial breathing space for an economy navigating global supply chain disruptions and political transition.
By deferring the immediate withdrawal of duty-free, quota-free (DFQF) market access, the decision protects Bangladeshi merchandise exports from an average tariff burden of 12.50% across 38 destination countries.
Yet, while industrial leaders breathe a sigh of relief, economic experts warn against treating this deferment as a license for delay.
The three-year grace period must not become a comfortable plateau, but rather an active launching pad for deep structural transformation, capacity building, and industrial modernization.
For Bangladesh’s flagship export sector—the readymade garment (RMG) industry—the deferment provides immediate tariff security in key markets across the European Union, United Kingdom, and regional trading blocs.
It buys vital time to negotiate bilateral trade agreements and preferential trade frameworks that can replace LDC-specific privileges after 2029.
Similarly, the local pharmaceutical sector gains temporary protection under the World Trade Organization’s TRIPS flexibilities.
This preserves local manufacturing rights for generic drugs and patented formulations without domestic price spikes on essential medicines like insulin and anti-retroviral treatments.
For non-exporting local industries—ranging from light engineering and consumer electronics to agriculture-linked processing—the temporary continuation of protective tariffs buys time to build scale and improve cost efficiency.
However, reliance on state support will become increasingly unsustainable as global trade rules require progressive tariff rationalization.
Capacity building imperative
The core challenge facing Bangladeshi industries over the next six years is no longer just tariff preferences—it is international competitiveness.
Modern trade buyers and import markets prioritize factory efficiency, regulatory compliance, and environmental standards over artificially subsidized prices.

Converting time into action
The extended timeline till November 2029 effectively provides Bangladesh with a total six-year buffer when factoring in post-graduation transition support.
However, past experience shows that long timelines without accountability often breed reform inertia.
To prevent history from repeating itself, the government must convert its Smooth Transition Strategy (STS) into a binding, time-bound policy roadmap.
Clear benchmarks, institutional accountability, and quarterly progress tracking will be necessary to ensure policy implementation keeps pace with international demands.
For private enterprises, the message is equally clear: government subsidies and trade protections will eventually end.
The true measure of success for this three-year extension will be determined not by the tariffs avoided today, but by the productivity, sustainability, and technological capabilities built for tomorrow.

item.title: Pakistani High Commissioner meets Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad
item.description:
Pakistani High Commissioner to Bangladesh Imran Haider paid a courtesy call on Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad at the latter’s office in the city on Sunday.
During the meeting at the National Parliament, the speaker thanked the government of Pakistan for supporting Barrister Jahrat Adib Chowdhury, chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Bangladesh Parliament, as a member of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) Executive Committee at the 153rd IPU Assembly held in Tanzania.
Both sides emphasized the importance of forming the parliamentary friendship group between Bangladesh and Pakistan and exchanging visits by parliamentary delegations.
They also exchanged views on providing training to officials and employees of the Bangladesh Parliament Secretariat at Pakistan's legislature, Majlis-e-Shoora.
The speaker invited the Pakistani high commissioner to observe the upcoming session of the Bangladesh Parliament, which will begin on November 09.
Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad, Bir Bikram, will visit Pakistan on November 23 at the invitation of the Speaker of Pakistan Parliament, according to a press release.

item.title: PM orders steps to protect garment workers’ interests, keep production uninterrupted
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday directed the authorities concerned to protect garment workers’ interests and ensure uninterrupted production and export activities in the apparel sector.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed came up with the prime minister’s instructions while talking to reporters after a meeting on the prevailing situation in the garment sector at the Secretariat at night.
At the same time, he warned that those involved in violence, sabotage and attempts to create disorder in the name of workers’ movement will be dealt with strictly.
“The prime minister has given advice and directives to ensure that garment workers’ interests are protected, their living standards improve, and production and development in Bangladesh are not disrupted, while exports increase. He has asked us to take steps keeping all these issues in consideration,” he said.
Salahuddin said the law enforcement agencies have been asked to take strict action against those who are involved in violence or attempting to create disorder and instability.
“We have asked the law enforcement agencies to deal firmly with those who are involved in violence, behaving recklessly or trying to create unnecessary disorder and instability,” he said.
The minister alleged that masked individuals infiltrated different levels of the incidents during the day and that some quarters from across the border were instigating innocent garment workers to create instability and disrupt the country's export trade and apparel production.
“Analysing the information available to the government, we have found that some people from across the border are instigating innocent garment workers to create instability in the country, disrupt export trade and hamper production in the garment industry,” he said.
The government will deal strictly with such activities, Salahuddin said, adding that those involved in violent acts are being brought under the law.
“Police and other law enforcement agencies will take strict action against any attempt at sabotage or creating disorder,” he added.
The minister said the government formed a wage board to revise the minimum wages of garment workers, stressing that there is no need for violent demonstrations as the issue can be resolved through discussions.
He said the law provides for the formation of a wage board every three years to review workers’ minimum wages. “Although there is time until December to form the board, the government has taken the initiative earlier through discussions with representatives of employers and workers.”
The employers had submitted the names of their representatives, but there was a delay in receiving nominations from workers’ organisations, Salahuddin said, adding that after receiving the worker representatives’ names on Saturday night, the government formed the board and issued a notification on Sunday morning.
The representatives of employers and workers on the board will discuss and recommend minimum wages, taking into account workers’ living standards, their ability to maintain a decent family life and their financial capacity, he said.
The minister said the government is sincere about protecting workers’ interests and improving their living standards.
He, however, alleged that violence took place in the name of the workers’ movement, including setting fire to police vehicles, attacks at different places, vandalism of vehicles and arson at factories. “There was no need for such violence when the issue of wages could be discussed and resolved through dialogue,” he said.
Salahuddin said the prime minister instructed the authorities concerned to ensure workers’ welfare and improve their living standards.
Tarique Rahman also advised the wage board and asked the Ministry of Labour and Employment to take necessary steps to protect workers’ interests, he said.
The government wants peace, discipline, development and progress, the minister said, adding that its goal is to expand the garment industry, increase export earnings and create more employment opportunities for workers.
He also recalled the contribution of Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman to the development of Bangladesh’s garment industry, saying the government wants the sector to grow further, exports to expand and employment opportunities to increase.
Asked whether factories closed amid the unrest will reopen on Monday, Salahuddin said garment factory owners have been urged to keep production running.
“If any factory has been closed for some reason, the closure should be temporary. Owners and workers should maintain normal production through mutual discussions and understanding,” he said.
The minister stressed that production and supply of goods for export must not be disrupted under any circumstances.
Asked when the wage board will hold its first meeting, he advised reporters to contact the board chairman for details.
The meeting began at 6pm at the Cabinet Division conference room of the Secretariat to review the situation surrounding the garment workers’ movement and clashes with police at different places.
Those present included Prime Minister’s Political Adviser Nazrul Islam Khan, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury, State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Mir Shahe Alam, Prime Minister’s Adviser Mahdi Amin and Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal Chief Coordinator Shamsur Rahman Shimul Biswas, MP.

item.title: Factory owners, former MP, former state minister, involved in RMG workers’ protests: Home Minister
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said, "Garment industry owners who are involved in the Awami League's ((activities banned) politics have also been working behind creating unrest. It is unfortunate that some industrialists are involved in this. Former MPs and state ministers are also involved."

This statement was made by the Home Minister in response to a question at a press conference after a meeting with the leaders of BGMEA and BKMEA, organisations of garment industry owners, at the Secretariat on Monday morning.

Informing that cooperation from garment factory owners was sought during the meeting, the Home Minister said some industrialists deliberately closed factories. The leaders of the owners' organisations have been asked to provide a list of them. At the same time, a list of worker leaders and organisations involved in creating unrest has been sought.

1 detained over ‘Facebook post’ about setting fire to police vehicle in Mirpur

The Home Minister mentioned that arrangements have been made for 24-hour surveillance to monitor the situation in the garment industry.

He said specific persons have been appointed for communication from the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Police Department. There will also be designated persons for communication from the owners' organisations.

For this, instructions have been given to establish a control room at the police headquarters. The situation will be monitored from there through security apps.

The Home Minister said, "We do not want any factory to close, not even for a moment."

The Minister stated that those who are engaged in anti-labour activities in the guise of labour movements and are trying to create instability in the country will be dealt with strictly.

He said legal action will be taken in this regard. No actual workers are involved in this unrest.

For the past few days, garment factory workers have been protesting demanding a minimum wage of Tk 30,000. To resolve the ongoing crisis, the Home Minister held a meeting with the leaders of BGMEA and BKMEA at the conference room of the Ministry of Home Affairs on Monday morning.

Speaking at a press conference after the meeting, the Home Minister alleged that for some time now, some supporters of fallen tyrannical fascism are using innocent workers to create unrest. Those who are trying to create unrest by blocking roads and highways and setting fires have been identified.

Garment workers try to take to the streets through Mirpur alleys, police disperse them

The Home Minister further said, "We would like to categorically state very sternly that those who are involved in anti-law enforcement activities under the guise of a labour movement, and those who are engaging in conspiracy to create instability in the country by creating unrest, will be sternly suppressed. Legal measures will be taken."

The Minister said that a few such individuals have been brought under the law today. He said video footage and some evidence of their activities have been collected. There are audios, videos, and visual video clips of various violent incidents.

The Minister said that the government has already formed a wage board. The first meeting of the board may be held today, he said. Even if not today, they will sit down within a very short time, and after discussion, the minimum wage will be determined and announced as soon as possible, he said.

Dhaka-Tangail highway blocked again by garment workers, BGB deployed

The Home Minister further said that the demand for setting up a Minimum Wage Board for workers every three years is something the government initiated weeks ago. The name of the representative from the owners' side was also provided. But the worker organisations took a few days to provide names. They provided the name of their representative the night before last. The Wage Board has been formed through a proper process by notification with names from both the worker and owner sides.

Meeting with labour union leaders in the afternoon

The Home Minister said that the government will meet with representatives of labour unions at around 3 PM today. The views and suggestions of the labour leaders will be heard there. Future steps will be taken based on their opinions.

Regarding the return of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to the country in the coming December, he said, "Fascist forces and fugitive leaders who want to return should do so quickly. Why should it take until December? We want to ensure justice by bringing them under the law swiftly."

Expatriate Welfare Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury, Prime Minister's Advisor Mahadi Amin, labour leader, and Member of Parliament Shimul Biswas were present at the press conference.

item.title: Cyclone ‘Murasu’ likely to cross south Andhra Pradesh coast by early 3 Nov: IMD
item.description:
ANI_20261101559

Cyclonic Storm Murasu intensified into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal and is likely to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between midnight on 2 November and the early hours of 3 November, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.

In its latest bulletin, the IMD said the system moved nearly northwestwards at a speed of 20 kmph during the past six hours and lay centred over the same region at 2:30 am IST on 2 November.

The severe cyclonic storm was centred near latitude 13.6°N and longitude 82.5°E, about 260 km east-northeast of Chennai, 290 km east-southeast of Nellore, 320 km south-southeast of Machilipatnam, 310 km east-southeast of Kavali, 330 km southeast of Ongole and 470 km south of Visakhapatnam.

The weather agency said the storm is very likely to continue moving northwestwards and cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast as a severe cyclonic storm, with a sustained wind speed of 100–110 kmph and gusts reaching 120 kmph.

The landfall is likely between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole, between 11:30 pm IST on 2 and 4 November am IST on 3 November, the IMD said.

Meanwhile, the Rayagada district administration has stepped up its preparedness for the possible impact of Cyclone Murasu, deploying all 11 fire station teams and heavy machinery at strategic locations for emergency response, Additional District Magistrate (General) Ravindranath Kahanra said.

The administration held a virtual emergency review meeting on Sunday under the chairmanship of the District Collector to assess preparedness for the possible cyclone and heavy rainfall.

The meeting reviewed early warning systems, emergency services, rescue and relief operations, shelter arrangements and the availability of essential equipment.

Speaking about the preparedness measures, Kahanra said, “In preparation for Cyclone Murasu, the Rayagada District Collector held a virtual emergency meeting to discuss safety measures and readiness. Key topics included the district's preparedness, early warning systems, emergency services, and shelter preparations.”

He said that, based on reports from the India Meteorological Department (IMD) and the Special Relief Commissioner (SRC), the district was under a yellow warning until 2 November, followed by an orange warning for 3 and 4 November.

The administration has deployed all 11 fire station teams and positioned JCBs, excavators and Hydra cranes at Gumma Ghati and Mukundpur Ghati for immediate clearance of National Highway 326 in case of road blockages.

Kahanra said, “The administration has deployed fire station teams and machinery for road clearance, while BDOs, Tahsildars and concerned officials have been instructed to remain present with all equipment and machinery to prepare for any type of eventuality.”
